NUS Coding Clinic — third-party front-end libraries
====================================================

These files are vendored (committed to the repo) on purpose: the site must work
from GitHub Pages with no build step, no npm, and no runtime CDN dependency. Nothing
here phones home.

Fetched: 2026-08-03  (marked, DOMPurify, highlight.js)  by agent A4 (api layer)
Fetched: 2026-08-08  (KaTeX + fonts)                    by agent F5 (rich content, v3 D8)

KaTeX — what was fetched, and the one edit made to it
-----------------------------------------------------
Exact commands (bash; re-runnable, the version is pinned in one place):

  V=0.18.1
  curl -sSf -o katex.min.js  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@$V/dist/katex.min.js
  curl -sSf -o katex.min.css https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@$V/dist/katex.min.css
  mkdir -p fonts
  for f in AMS-Regular Caligraphic-Bold Caligraphic-Regular Fraktur-Bold Fraktur-Regular \
           Main-Bold Main-BoldItalic Main-Italic Main-Regular Math-BoldItalic Math-Italic \
           SansSerif-Bold SansSerif-Italic SansSerif-Regular Script-Regular \
           Size1-Regular Size2-Regular Size3-Regular Size4-Regular Typewriter-Regular; do
    curl -sSf -o "fonts/KaTeX_$f.woff2" \
      "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@$V/dist/fonts/KaTeX_$f.woff2"
  done

THE ONE EDIT: upstream katex.min.css lists three sources per @font-face —
.woff2, .woff and .ttf — which is 60 font files, ~2.3 MB, for a repo that only
ever needs the first. Every `,url(fonts/KaTeX_*.woff) format("woff")` and
`,url(fonts/KaTeX_*.ttf) format("truetype")` was deleted, leaving the .woff2
source alone. Nothing else in the file was touched (24,727 B -> 22,593 B).
woff2 is supported everywhere this site is supported. If you ever restore the
other two formats you must also fetch the 40 extra font files, or every formula
silently falls back to a system serif.

The layout `assets/vendor/katex.min.css` + `assets/vendor/fonts/` is NOT
negotiable: KaTeX's CSS resolves `url(fonts/…)` relative to the stylesheet.

WATCH THE Size1..Size4 FONTS. They are easy to miss when listing the font names
by hand because they are the only ones with a digit in them, and they are what
draws \sum, \int, \sqrt and any \left( \right) that has to stretch. Miss them
and math renders, looks fine at a glance, and every big operator is wrong. The
count to check against is 20 .woff2 files and 20 `url(` references in the CSS.

markdown.js does NOT put KaTeX in the marked pipeline, and must never be
"fixed" to. See the long comment at the top of markdown.js: DOMPurify FORBIDs
`math` and `svg` and STRIPs `style`, and katex output is all inline `style`, so
a marked extension is silently mangled with no error at all. Math is typeset on
the live DOM after sanitisation, inside Clinic.md.enhance().

highlight.js build
------------------
This is the official "common" CDN bundle (cdn-release build/highlight.min.js), which
registers 36 grammars. Verified present in this exact file:

  bash, c, cpp, csharp, css, diff, go, graphql, ini, java, javascript, json, kotlin,
  less, lua, makefile, markdown, objectivec, perl, php, php-template, plaintext,
  python, python-repl, r, ruby, rust, scss, shell, sql, swift, typescript, vbnet,
  wasm, xml, yaml

The three that matter for this course — python, bash, json — are all in. So are r, sql,
markdown, yaml and diff, which covers everything students are likely to paste.

No highlight.js theme CSS is vendored. The `.hljs-*` token classes are styled by
site/assets/css/main.css (agent A1) so that code blocks follow the site's light/dark
theme toggle instead of shipping two extra stylesheets.

Upgrading
---------
Replace the file with the same-named build from the same CDN path at a newer version,
then update the version + size above. Check afterwards that:
  * marked      — still exposes a global `marked` with `.parse(md, {gfm, breaks})`
  * DOMPurify   — still exposes a global `DOMPurify` with `.sanitize()` and `.addHook()`
  * highlight.js— still exposes a global `hljs` with `.highlightElement()`, and still
                  includes python/bash/json (open the file and search for `grmr_python`)
  * KaTeX       — still exposes a global `katex` with `.renderToString(tex, opts)`, and
                  `output:'html'` still suppresses the MathML half. Check with:
                    node -e "var k=require('./katex.min.js');
                             var h=k.renderToString('\\frac12',{output:'html',throwOnError:false});
                             console.log(/<math/.test(h), /style=/.test(h))"
                  It must print `false true`. If <math> ever appears in the html output,
                  DOMPurify is not the problem — nothing sanitises it — but the aria-label
                  fallback in markdown.js's mathNode() becomes the only accessible name,
                  which it already is. Also re-check the font list (20 .woff2).
assets/js/markdown.js degrades to plain escaped <pre> text if any of the three globals
is missing, so a bad upgrade cannot white-screen the site — it just loses formatting.

Mirrors, in the order they were tried
-------------------------------------
1. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/...   <- all three came from here
2. https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/...
3. https://unpkg.com/...
